weaknesses: The central performance evidence has a fundamental synchronization concern. The timing protocol does not specify how all streams are synchronized. Consequently, the reported gains could reflect unmeasured asynchronous work rather than faster completed computation. Repeated measurements cannot correct this systematic error.

The supplied code contradicts the claimed executability and undermines the case-study ablations. Table 16 performs its first-use convolution on a 4×4×4 dummy input with the specified 3×5×7 kernel and zero padding, which cannot execute. In Table 15, disabling 'reduced branching' introduces repeated debug printing, confounding the claimed contribution of branch reduction. These concrete issues are not reconciled with the reported correctness checks.

Generalization to unseen kernels is unsupported. Section 2.2 explicitly uses all 250 KernelBench tasks to generate fine-tuning data, and the same tasks supply the headline evaluation. No held-out tasks or workload families are evaluated. Running the resulting programs on different GPUs establishes hardware portability, not learned optimization of unseen kernels.

Comparisons do not isolate the proposed method fairly. Vanilla models receive five attempts, while evolutionary and CUDA-L1 search budgets and final candidate-selection procedures are unspecified. A frozen model after the same SFT/self-training stages with matched evolutionary search is needed to isolate contrastive RL. Comparisons against torch.compile and straightforward CUDA-graph/cuDNN configurations are also missing.

Reproducibility is substantially inadequate for training a 671B-parameter backbone. The manuscript omits learning rates, optimizer settings, training steps, GRPO group size and numerical hyperparameters, parameter-update strategy, search budgets, and total compute. It also lacks an executable evaluation harness, numerical tolerances despite enabling TF32, and sufficient details to audit reward-hacking prevention beyond prompt instructions.

The methodological novelty is overstated. The core algorithm is standard GRPO with performance-scored evolutionary exemplars in the prompt, rather than a new contrastive objective. Moreover, subtracting the common mean in Equation 1 cancels exactly under softmax and does not create the claimed distinct sampling distribution. Claims about discovering new optimization principles require stronger evidence than the technically problematic case studies.

The headline 17.7× arithmetic mean is heavily influenced by extreme results, whereas the median is 1.81×. The largest recurrent-network and convolution gains are precisely those affected by the synchronization concerns. Without corrected measurements, absolute runtimes, and uncertainty estimates, neither the headline acceleration nor the claimed practical impact is established.
